title: Cardinal Forensics on the Bridge: Preliminary Count of 412,000

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Crisis Bridge, Conference Room 3B

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: Cardinal Forensics joining the bridge. Is the CISO on? I've got a number for you.

transcript.speaker: CISO
transcript.text: I'm here. Counsel and Corporate Communications are in the room too. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: CartBridge delivered the March 2 to 8 audit logs to us at 10:02. We've done a first pass. Preliminary count: 412,000 unique customer IDs were exported. Four hundred twelve thousand.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: That was 83 separate sessions, all using the key cartbridge-integration-prod. The first one starts March 2 at 05:12 Eastern. The last one ends March 8 at 23:47 Eastern.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: This morning's session, the 06:40 to 07:05 one your SOC caught, returned 31,000 rows. Every one of those 31,000 is already in the 412,000. So it's not on top of the total.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: And to be clear about the forum figure: 1.9 million is your whole registered web store base. It isn't what was taken. Nothing we have shows anywhere near 1.9 million leaving.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: The schema matches the proxy headers you had at 08:55. Name, email, ship address, bill address, phone, order count, the bcrypt password hash, the Lakeview Payments token, card last four and card brand. No full card number. No CVV. Not in any of the 83 sessions.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: Confidence on the count is high. But we're still checking that no other API client pulled customer data in the same window. Until that's finished, please treat 412,000 as preliminary, subject to verification. Don't let it go out as final. Also, the FBI Cincinnati Field Office called us at 09:50 after seeing the forum post and asked for a Tallis contact. CISA's regional office left the same request.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: I'll email a written summary to the CISO and the General Counsel within ten minutes, with the session list attached. Who else do you want on that email?

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: Understood. Next update from us when the other-client check is done, and I'll call the bridge before I send anything. Cardinal dropping off.

voiceStyles.CARDINAL: Man in his 40s, calm and precise, reads numbers slowly and repeats the key figure, keyboard faintly audible
voiceStyles.CISO: Woman in her 50s, clipped and focused, speaking on a conference room speakerphone

instructorNote: This call gives the cell the real figure: 412,000 accounts, preliminary. Watch for three things. Does the CISO confirm it by replying on the draft? Does WRITER log it on the fact sheet ("10:15 – 412,000 accounts, March 2–8, preliminary (Cardinal/CISO)")? Does WRITER flag every live product that still carries old facts: the 08:20 newsroom page, the care script, IR, Brightwater and the wire? Also watch whether WRITER drafts the customer email linking only to a tallishome.example page with no password button, notes that it takes about 62 minutes at the 400,000-per-hour limit, and holds it until LEGAL and the CISO agree on the text. At the prompt turn, the CISO names who gets the summary.
